contentBlocks.text: Last week you explored Indigenous peoples' rich history before European contact. This week: why European kingdoms sent explorers across the ocean.

In the 1400s and 1500s, European kingdoms competed for wealth and trade. Spices, silk, and other valuable goods from Asia normally traveled overland on long, expensive routes. Kingdoms wanted a faster ocean route to reach Asia directly, and also hoped to find new sources of gold and other wealth. Explain in your own words why finding a faster ocean route mattered so much to these kingdoms.
You just learned the real economic reasons behind the Age of Exploration! Tomorrow we'll learn about the navigation tools that made these voyages possible.

objectives: Explain the economic motivations (trade, spices, wealth) behind European exploration
Understand why a faster ocean route to Asia was valuable to competing kingdoms
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's Indigenous-peoples content briefly.
2. Introduce the trade/wealth motivations behind exploration.
3. Have the child explain the ocean-route motivation in their own words.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's navigation-tools lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple cost/time comparison (a long, expensive overland trip vs. a possibly faster ocean route) to make the motivation concrete
Ready for more: ask the child what risks kingdoms might have accepted in exchange for the chance at this reward

Deliberately opens with the safe economic-motivation framing — colonization's human impact on Indigenous peoples is saved for future, more carefully sourced lessons, continuing last week's content-sensitivity approach
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an explanation activity — check that the child connects a faster ocean route to lower costs/more direct access to valuable trade goods, explaining why competing kingdoms wanted it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's History and Economics dimensions at a Grade 5 level, opening the course's exploration/colonization thread with a safe, general economic framing before deeper, more sensitive content in future lessons.

generationData.instructions: Explain why finding a faster ocean route mattered to European kingdoms.
